title: Option to choose which device's battery is shown in the CompactRepresentation
line: The Power and Battery icon's context menu now has a Show on Icon section to show a mouse, gamepad or other device's battery on the icon.
explanation: The Power and Battery icon always showed the combined internal battery, or the power mode icon on computers without one, so the level of a wireless mouse or gamepad was only visible after opening the popup. The battery model also had no stable identifier per device, so a choice could not be stored. The battery model now exposes each battery's UPower path, and the applet's context menu gets a 'Show on Icon' section (Internal Battery or Power Mode, plus each peripheral) that makes the icon, percentage badge and tooltip follow the chosen device; it falls back to the normal icon while that device is disconnected.

commits.message:
components/batterycontrol: expose each battery's UPower path

The battery model gave no stable way to tell its batteries apart, so an
applet could not remember a chosen device. Add a Udi role with the UPower
object path, which the battery applet uses to show a chosen battery.

BUG: 526188

applets/batterymonitor: allow choosing which battery the icon shows

The icon only showed the internal batteries, or the power mode on desktops
without one, so a mouse or gamepad level needed a click. A new Show on Icon
section in the context menu now lets the icon show one of those devices.

BUG: 526188

media.caption: Context menu on a desktop with a mouse and a gamepad: no way to choose a device
New Show on Icon section; the mouse is chosen and the icon shows its low battery
Panel icon on a desktop without internal battery: a generic icon, tooltip says nothing about the devices
With the mouse chosen, the icon shows its charge level and the tooltip names it
System tray: the battery item is hidden in the overflow
System tray copy set to the gamepad: shown in the tray with the gamepad's level

review.text: A small, clean model addition (Udi role) plus a 'Show on Icon' radio section that fits the applet, whose only setting already lives in its context menu. Each widget keeps its own choice, and the icon falls back to the normal one while the device is absent. The media show the menu, the icon, the tooltip and the tray copy. Known limits are acceptable: UPower paths like hidpp_battery_N can change between boots, and the menu order depends on Instantiator pushing into contextualActions. It adds new strings, so it goes to master only.
